items.body:
<details open>

GDN: use replay instead of rollback (#31669)

* GDN: use replay instead of rollback [WIP]

* memory : move rs_max with the sequence when find_slot swaps cells

find_slot swapped pos/src/rs_pend/seq_id of the cell it moves out of the
way, but not rs_max, so that sequence inherited the rollback depth of the
cell's previous owner. A smaller value made seq_rm refuse the rollback
(#31656), a larger one made snapshot mode restore the previous owner's
snapshots.

With rs_replay the pending columns are copied along with the state, so
rs_max follows the sequence. Without it only the final state is copied and
the snapshots stay behind, so the moved sequence gets rs_max 0.

* delta_net: drop the graph replay fallback

The graph fallback ran the replay as two gdn ops and copied the
committed state from the replay gdn when keep, from the main gdn
otherwise. Backends whose graph_optimize reorders nodes (Metal,
Vulkan) then give keep and non keep ubatches a different node order
for the same node count, and the scheduler reallocates on every
switch (abort under GGML_SCHED_DEBUG_REALLOC).

The replay now always runs in the gdn op. A device without the replay
in its gdn op leaves the op to the CPU through the scheduler, as for
any unsupported op. This removes LLAMA_RS_REPLAY=2, the replay probe,
rs_replay_fused and the rep_mask input.

* metal: replay the pending gated delta net tokens in the kernel

The gated delta net kernel replays the pending tokens of each seq
before the new ones, with the same state update as the main loop and
no attention output. With keep, it writes the state after the replay
and skips the final state.

The replay is a function constant of the pipeline, keep is a kernel
argument as on CUDA. The pending buffers fall back to src0 when the
op has no

<details open>

opencl: fetch the Adreno binary kernel library at configure time for Windows on Snapdragon (#31759)

* opencl: fetch the Adreno binary kernel library at configure time

Make GGML_OPENCL_USE_ADRENO_BIN_KERNELS an option, default ON, and add
GGML_OPENCL_ADRENO_BIN_KERNELS_FETCH, default ON. On Windows, CMake
downloads the pinned adreno-opencl-kernels release from the Qualcomm
Software Center, verifies its SHA256, and copies the DLL and its license
next to the executables. A failed download is only a warning; the
backend then uses its builtin kernels.

The opencl-adreno release job turns the fetch off, since it ships only
ggml-opencl.dll.

* opencl: fetch the Adreno binary kernel library only on ARM64

The library is built for Windows on ARM64 only.

* opencl: add download timeout and better handle output dir

Assisted-by: Codex

* opencl: add .txt to license file

Assisted-by: Codex

---------

Co-authored-by: Li He <lih@qti.qualcomm.com>

</details>

metal : batch concat rows and copy them in vector chunks (#32824)

* metal : batch concat rows and copy them in vector chunks

The concat kernel copied one element per thread, so wide rows with many rows ran at a
fraction of the memory bandwidth. Batch several rows per threadgroup and copy the
contiguous dim-0 elements in 4-element chunks when the row is contiguous.

Assisted-by: dsh:llama.cpp/ggml-org/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-GGUF (Mac Studio, M5 Ultra, 256GB)

* test : cover concat vector and misaligned row paths

Assisted-by: dsh:llama.cpp/ggml-org/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF (RTX 5090 32GB, DDR5 128GB)

* metal : hoist the concat src1 row offset into scalars

Assisted-by: dsh:llama.cpp/ggml-org/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF (RTX 5090 32GB, DDR5 128GB)

* metal : peel to align the concat vector copy

Assisted-by: dsh:llama.cpp/ggml-org/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF (RTX 5090 32GB, DDR5 128GB)

* metal : vectorize concat rows along any dimension

Assisted-by: dsh:llama.cpp/ggml-org/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF (RTX 5090 32GB, DDR5 128GB)

* metal : specialize concat with function constants

Assisted-by: dsh:llama.cpp/ggml-org/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF (RTX 5090 32GB, DDR5 128GB)

* metal : drop the concat row-batch dispatch

Batching several rows per threadgroup reduces the number of threads by
the batch factor. On machines with a large GPU this leaves too few
requests in flight and the copy becomes latency bound:

  M5 Ultra (36 CPU)   f16 [1024,8,256,1] d=0   8.1 us -> 17.2 us
                      f32 [4096,8,256,1] d=0  35.4 us -> 118.5 us
                      f16 [4096,8,256,1] d=2  50.9 us -> 102.0 us

An interleaved sweep of the (nth, nrptg) dispatch over the concat perf
cases on an M2 Ultra and an M5 Ultra shows that the base dispatch is
